import json, subprocess, sys, hashlib
def mv(mid,side,speaker,sec,kind,claim,warrant,inference,start,end,quotes,conf,ar,av,imp,ir,bridge,tier,br,responds=[],components=[]):
 return {"moveId":mid,"side":side,"speaker":speaker,"sectionId":sec,"moveKind":kind,"claim":claim,"warrant":warrant,"inference":inference,"startEvent":start,"endEvent":end,"sourceSpanSelectionRationale":"The span begins with the stated contention and ends after its supporting reason and resulting inference are complete.","quoteEligibleExactSpans":quotes,"attributionConfidence":conf,"attributionRationale":ar,"audioVerificationReason":av,"importance":imp,"importanceRationale":ir,"burdenContact":{"bridgeId":bridge,"tier":tier,"rationale":br},"respondsToIds":responds,"responseComponents":components}
moves=[
mv("causal-history-behind-intent","con","Robert Sapolsky","causal-origin-of-choice","constructive","Intent and conscious choice do not establish free will because the relevant question is how the agent became disposed to form that intent.","Ordinary choices arise from a person whose dispositions have prior causes; considering only the final conscious moment is like reviewing only the last minutes of a film.","Responsibility cannot be grounded merely in uncoerced intention without accounting for the causal formation of the chooser.",67,113,["Where did that intent come from?"],"high","The moderator hands the floor to Sapolsky and first-person continuity is clear.","",3,"This states Sapolsky’s central burden against free will.","con-causal-origin","motion","Directly argues that ordinary choosing does not meet the motion-level requirement for free will."),
mv("multiscale-biological-development","con","Robert Sapolsky","causal-origin-of-choice","constructive","Behavioral dispositions reflect interacting immediate states, development, culture, fetal conditions, genes, and environment.","Sapolsky traces effects from hunger and hormones through trauma, childhood, culture, fetal development, and gene-environment interaction.","If these layers causally shape judgment and self-control, the final choice cannot be isolated as an independently authored act.",146,283,["Genes determine next to nothing."],"high","Continuous opening speech with no speaker handoff.","",3,"This supplies the empirical framework for the con case.","con-causal-origin","central","Connects the denial of free will to a continuous causal account rather than simple genetic determinism."),
mv("continuous-arc-no-gap","con","Robert Sapolsky","burden-and-definition","constructive","The known biological and environmental history forms a continuous causal arc with no demonstrated opening for free will.","The same causal story connects evolution, fetal regulation, recent protein activity, personality, desires, and behavior.","Until an action independent of that history is shown, Sapolsky says the default should be doubt about free will.",284,336,["It forms one continuous arc of biology","the onus is on the free will believers"],"high","The conclusion closes Sapolsky’s opening and is supported by the supplementary audio text.","",3,"This explicitly states his motion-level inference and burden.","con-no-independent-gap","motion","Places the evidential burden on showing independence from biological and environmental history."),
mv("reasons-responsiveness-shows-capacity","pro","Daniel Dennett","burden-and-definition","constructive","The ability to give and respond to reasons is evidence of the kind of free will worth defending.","Both debaters try to persuade because people can be receptive to reasons, while Dennett accepts the unequal biological and developmental starting material.","A causally formed person can still possess a real reasons-responsive capacity, so determinism alone does not defeat free will.",343,390,["we are both receptive to reasons"],"high","The moderator explicitly hands the floor to Dennett and his first-person argument is continuous.","",3,"This defines the central compatibilist burden.","pro-reasons-responsive-control","motion","Identifies the capacity Dennett claims satisfies the motion under determinism."),
mv("evolved-skill-of-self-control","pro","Daniel Dennett","evolved-self-control","constructive","Free will is an evolved and socially cultivated skill of self-control rather than an uncaused metaphysical power.","Evolution develops competence, and civilization refines skills that make people reliable and able to prevent foreseeable harm.","Degrees of foresight and self-control ground meaningful differences in responsible agency.",402,462,["Free will is an achievement. It’s a skill."],"high","Dennett continues uninterrupted through the evolutionary and skill argument.","",3,"This is the main constructive account of free will.","pro-evolved-capacity","central","Explains how deterministic evolution can produce the relevant capacity."),
mv("diminished-capacity-thresholds","pro","Daniel Dennett","responsibility-and-exceptions","constructive","Responsible agency admits diminished-capacity exceptions and practical thresholds.","Some people lack enough self-control to make contracts or act safely, and age or impairment can justify treating them as not responsible.","Acknowledging luck and impairment does not erase the capacity in people who meet a workable threshold.",463,504,[],"high","Continuous first-person speech with clear examples and no mixed ownership.","",2,"This qualifies the pro position and prevents universal attribution.","pro-thresholded-responsibility","subsidiary","Shows how the account handles unequal capacities and exceptions."),
mv("civilization-reduces-cruel-punishment","pro","Daniel Dennett","social-consequences","constructive","Civilization can improve responsibility practices by abandoning horrific punishment while retaining fair social regulation.","Dennett cites the historical rejection of torture and religiously loaded guilt as moral progress.","A humane responsibility system is compatible with free will understood as cultivated self-control.",515,530,[],"high","Dennett owns the passage; the examples are presented as his historical claims.","",2,"This connects his view to the practical stakes raised by Sapolsky.","pro-humane-accountability","subsidiary","Supports a non-barbaric form of accountability."),
mv("determined-will-is-desirable","pro","Daniel Dennett","burden-and-definition","constructive","A valuable will should be determined by facts and values, not be undetermined.","Dennett argues that no desirable purpose has been shown for an undetermined will.","Therefore incompatibilist indeterminism is unnecessary for the free will people should care about.",534,567,["We want our will to be determined by the facts and by our values."],"high","Dennett’s closing constructive point is continuous and clearly attributed.","",3,"This directly rejects the rival standard of freedom.","pro-determinism-compatible","central","Explains why determinism is compatible with, and can support, controlled agency."),

mv("self-control-itself-is-caused","con","evolved-self-control","evolved-self-control","reply","Self-control is itself a biological trait whose development depends on circumstances outside the agent’s control.","Sapolsky locates self-control in prefrontal development and gives parental socioeconomic status as an early predictor of that development.","Treating self-control as the basis of free will does not escape the causal-history problem.",671,736,["self-control is as biological of a trait as is your eye color"],"high","The reply remains Sapolsky’s uninterrupted first-person argument.","",3,"This directly contests Dennett’s central account.","con-self-control-caused","central","Answers the evolved-capacity case by tracing the capacity’s own unchosen causes.",["evolved-skill-of-self-control","diminished-capacity-thresholds"],[{"targetMoveId":"evolved-skill-of-self-control","description":"Argues that the proposed skill is itself causally produced."},{"targetMoveId":"diminished-capacity-thresholds","description":"Challenges limiting causal exemption to conspicuous impairment cases."}]),
mv("responsibility-removal-as-progress","con","Robert Sapolsky","social-consequences","reply","Expanding causal understanding has repeatedly reduced blame and made society more humane.","Examples involving alleged witchcraft, epilepsy, dyslexia, schizophrenia, and obesity illustrate cases where causal explanation displaced moral condemnation.","This pattern supports extending reduced desert rather than preserving responsibility for ordinary cases by default.",787,839,[],"high","The long reply is continuous and examples are clearly presented as Sapolsky’s evidence.","",3,"This is Sapolsky’s principal consequences argument.","con-humane-consequences","central","Links causal explanation to reduced blame and humane treatment."),
mv("quotation-context-rebuttal","pro","Daniel Dennett","quotation-and-model-dispute","reply","Sapolsky’s runner and two-stage quotations do not establish Dennett’s endorsement of the positions attributed to him.","Dennett says the runner passage continues by rejecting the quoted idea, and the two-stage article rejects that model while noting only that it meets an intuition.","The textual challenges therefore cannot bear the argumentative weight Sapolsky assigns them without their stated context.",844,881,["the whole point of that article is to say the two-stage model doesn’t work"],"high","The reply handoff is explicit and supplementary audio confirms the context claims; textual accuracy remains speaker-reported.","",2,"This answers two distinct but linked source-based attacks.","pro-contextual-rebuttal","subsidiary","Defends the pro account against attributed positions he says he rejected.",[],[]),
mv("deterministic-chaos-and-autonomy","pro","Daniel Dennett","evolved-self-control","reply","Determinism need not imply predictability or external controllability, and responsible agents can acquire limited autonomy.","Dennett invokes chaotic, hard-to-predict neural processes and says people can become able to resist manipulation despite not being responsible for becoming such agents.","Deterministic origins are compatible with a present capacity to maintain autonomy and respond to influence selectively.",892,961,["You can maintain your autonomy","natural selection works fine with deterministic chaos"],"high","Dennett speaks continuously; the coin-flip wording is preserved without forcing a stronger claim.","",3,"This is the principal reply to causal-history determinism.","pro-determinism-compatible","central","Distinguishes causal determination from predictability and control by others.",["continuous-arc-no-gap"],[{"targetMoveId":"continuous-arc-no-gap","description":"Argues that a continuous deterministic history can still produce autonomy."}]),
mv("chooser-values-remain-unchosen","con","Robert Sapolsky","quotation-and-model-dispute","reply","Generating options and then choosing among them does not create free will because the chooser’s values and priorities were not self-chosen.","Sapolsky accepts option generation and filtering but asks how the agent became the person who ranks one option above another.","The two-stage description returns to the same causal-origin question rather than answering it.",964,999,["You did not choose to become the sort of person"],"high","The moderator invites Sapolsky directly, and his short answer is continuous.","",3,"This is the con side’s direct answer within the final reply round.","con-unchosen-chooser","central","Targets the remaining locus of choice after option generation.",["deterministic-chaos-and-autonomy"],[{"targetMoveId":"deterministic-chaos-and-autonomy","description":"Accepts generated options but denies that selection among them is self-originating."}]),
mv("education-builds-responsible-capacity","pro","Daniel Dennett","responsibility-and-exceptions","reply","Education and treatment can counteract causal disadvantages and help many people acquire responsible agency.","Dennett agrees that no one is ultimately responsible for their starting conditions, but argues that social practices can remediate some conditions and excuse those that cannot be remedied.","A socially produced capacity can still be real and can justify responsibility for those who possess it.",1001,1039,["Some people don’t have free will.","they hold themselves responsible"],"high","Dennett resumes after Sapolsky’s answer; first-person continuity and the formal-round boundary are clear.","",3,"This completes the compatibilist answer while retaining exceptions.","pro-thresholded-responsibility","central","Connects causal luck, remediation, and differentiated responsibility.",["self-control-itself-is-caused"],[{"targetMoveId":"self-control-itself-is-caused","description":"Concedes causal formation but argues that education and treatment can create the relevant capacity."}]),
mv("fair-nonawful-sanction-system","pro","Daniel Dennett","social-consequences","reply","A functioning civilization needs sanctions, ideally administered through a fair and non-awful system.","Dennett says law and order require punishment and immediately qualifies the ideal system as fair and minimally harmful.","His compatibilist view aims to preserve protection and accountability without cruel retribution.",1040,1052,[],"high","The formal reply boundary is confirmed by supplementary audio; the final recognition-corrupted clause is excluded from quotation and interpretation.","",2,"This states the practical endpoint of the pro account.","pro-humane-accountability","subsidiary","Shows the institutional role assigned to responsibility.",["instrumental-sanctions-agreed"],[{"targetMoveId":"instrumental-sanctions-agreed","description":"Builds on the shared acceptance of instrumental sanctions while retaining responsibility language."}])
